recording.starts: fresh install, on the first story screen (no splash captured; 'Have an account? Login' top right)
recording.paywall_at: 4:14 (trial-reminder gate with no price; the first price appears at 4:22.7 on Rise's own web checkout in Chrome)
recording.after_paywall: Tester opened Apple Pay for the $0.99 month, closed it unpaid, swiped back to the app and found a second, in-app paywall with no close button; opened and closed the money-back guarantee; no discount or exit offer; recording ends at 4:57 on that paywall.

strategy: RISE sells a diagnosis before a product: it reframes sleep as a free performance drug, then spends four minutes turning the person's answers and Apple Health history into their own numbers (sleep need, 10 hours of sleep debt, 50% energy, a morning peak and tonight's melatonin window), narrated by an AI persona they chose. The arc runs from curiosity, through a clinical-style self-assessment where every admission is rewarded with a tailored line, into relief (energy is a pattern, not willpower), then concern at the debt figure and ownership as they confirm readings and add a reminder to their schedule. By the paywall the plan feels built and already started, so price is framed as 'one last step' and the in-app paywall locks tomorrow's guidance. The carrying idea is that sleep debt is the one number that explains how you feel, and only RISE can measure it and pay it down.

phases.name: Story hook
phases.goal: Make sleep feel like an undervalued performance drug and Rise the science-based way to use it, so the person starts the questionnaire curious and with low resistance.

phases.name: Introductions and basics
phases.goal: Start a personal relationship (the name is greeted back and reused) and collect demographics, each with a short reason why it matters.

phases.name: Goals and sleep self-assessment
phases.goal: Get the person to name goals and rate their sleep problems on a clinical-style scale, while every answer is met with a line written for it, so admitting problems feels rewarded rather than judged.

phases.name: Habits and health screen
phases.goal: Remove the 'I need a wearable' objection, turn existing habits into promised features and quietly collect apnea-risk data, deepening the sense that the plan fits their life.

phases.name: AI Expert calibration
phases.goal: Introduce an AI companion the person chooses, reframe low energy as a solvable pattern rather than willpower, and have the persona read back their answers and commit to a plan, so they feel known and accompanied.

phases.name: Data permissions
phases.goal: Secure motion, Health, tracking and notification access while the person is primed by 'discover my patterns', and keep goodwill when they decline.

phases.name: Personal numbers
phases.goal: Convert data access into the person's own results (sleep need, 10 hours of sleep debt, 50% energy) and install sleep debt as the one number that explains how they feel.

phases.name: Guided day walkthrough
phases.goal: Walk through their own day with the persona, collecting small confirmations and one schedule addition, so they experience the product working and end with an action for tonight.

phases.name: Pre-paywall promise and proof
phases.goal: Lift from personal data to a transformation promise and peer proof immediately before the trial ask.

phases.name: Trial and paywall
phases.goal: Defuse trial anxiety, then sell a free trial into an annual plan, first on Rise's web checkout and then in-app, framing payment as the last step of a plan that is already theirs and locking its future days.

intermission_pattern: Most of RISE's intermission work is done inline rather than on separate screens: 13 of the first 26 questions answer each picked option with a line written for it (a promise, a user stat, or an absolution such as 'That's alright...'), so the questionnaire carries its own validation. Stand-alone intermissions cluster at boundaries: a six-screen opener (riddle, benefit list, reframe, promise, low-effort section intro, scale proof), a name mirror, one reassurance card after the wearable question that closes the self-assessment, an AI-expert intro at the 1:30 fatigue point, a science absolution right after the fatalistic 'Just how I'm built', the persona greeting, and a no-guilt screen after notifications are declined. In the questionnaire that is roughly one stand-alone intermission every 6 to 8 questions; in the reveal the rhythm becomes one-line education beats between numbers (what sleep debt is, why it matters) and then the persona's typed cards, which mirror earlier answers ('new baby' twice) and alternate with one-tap check-ins. Tone is calm, second person and science-flavoured, colour-coded by section (purple profile, yellow AI, orange challenges, green energy). Collectively they build one belief: your own data holds the answer, and the answer is a debt you can pay down.
standouts: Screen 37: the chosen AI persona types a summary that weaves two unrelated earlier answers (Limiting screen time, New baby) into one natural sentence, asks a follow-up, then lays out a three-part plan, the strongest 'it actually listened' moment in the flow.

Screen 31: 'Your energy isn't a willpower thing. It's a pattern with a cause.' appears right after the person answers that low energy is 'Just how I'm built', a textbook absolution placed at the exact moment of fatalism (one run cannot show whether it is conditional on that answer).

Screens 15 to 21 are the seven Insomnia Severity Index items, each answered inline, so 'Dissatisfied' gets 'That's alright, sounds like there is a lot of room for improvement' and a clinical screener feels supportive rather than diagnostic.

Screen 60: mid-onboarding the app puts a Live Activity on the lock screen saying 'Half your Sleep Window is set' and 'a few more clicks for the rest', an open loop that follows the person outside the app.

A fourth AI Expert card to the left of Hunter was only partly visible and its name is unreadable. The goals list below 'Reduce anxiety' was never scrolled into view. The melatonin reminder card (screen 64) was tapped while still typing, so its last sentence is cut off. No new frames between 0:53 and 0:58.7 or 1:24 and 1:30.7 (tester paused). The 10 hrs sleep debt did not visibly change after the tester cut sleep need to 3h 25m. Why the in-app trial reminder toggle switched off at 4:44 is not visible. Personal payment and contact details on the Apple Pay sheet are deliberately left out. No mechanism names were added beyond the list.
